- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect risk reversal.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use 3-period moving average to smooth.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model tends to lag; add 1–2% lag correction to forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; apply sentiment smoothing (e.g., 5-day average) before forecasting.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model may misalign with trend; align forecast to sentiment median over 5–7 days instead of latest.
